# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (only artifact in the evidence folder — no separate IDS/alert export was provided). LAN: `10.2.28.0/24`, gateway/DC `10.2.28.2` (AD domain `easyas123.tech`, NetBIOS `EASYAS123`).

## Victim host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 | conversations, ARP |
| MAC address | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.2.28.88`) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR | NBNS `<00>` records, DHCP option 12 |
| Logged-in user | **brolf** | Kerberos `CNameString` on AS-REQ traffic between 10.2.28.88 and the DC (10.2.28.2) |

## Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (NetSupport Manager remote-access tool abused as a commodity RAT). Attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral: the C2 HTTP traffic carries the literal headers `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` (client→server) and `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)` (server→client), with the native NetSupport client protocol commands `CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encoded blob>` visible in plaintext inside the HTTP bodies (TCP stream 40, and all subsequent streams to the same C2). The malware speaks its C2 protocol as HTTP POSTs to `/fakeurl.htm` over TCP/443 without TLS, a known evasion trick to blend outbound traffic with the port that is normally allowed through egress firewalls for HTTPS.

The pcap begins with the C2 channel already active (first `vadusa.xyz` DNS lookup at t=44.77s, first C2 POST at t=44.89s), so the initial delivery/infection vector (phishing lure, exploit, dropped loader) is not captured in this evidence and cannot be reported.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Command-and-control:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` (TCP) — NetSupport RAT C2, plaintext HTTP-over-443, POST `/fakeurl.htm`, 264 beacon POSTs from 10.2.28.88:51912 spanning t=44.9s to t=15682.3s (~4.4 hours), i.e. persistent beaconing for the life of the capture.

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolved by 10.2.28.88 at t=44.77s to A record `45.131.214.85`, the C2 IP. (The malware then connects directly to the bare IP for all subsequent traffic — no further DNS lookups for this domain.)

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — C2 checkin/tasking endpoint, repeated POST requests.

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None. All HTTP object exports from this capture (`--export-objects http`) resolve to legitimate Microsoft/Adobe update artifacts (`ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `armmf.adobe.com`) — no executable, archive, or other payload was transferred in-capture. The C2 body content (`DATA=...`) is encoded/encrypted NetSupport protocol traffic, not a recoverable file.

**Benign context (not indicators):** Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update traffic (`ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `edge.microsoft.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `ocsp.digicert.com`), Adobe ARM check-in (`armmf.adobe.com`, `acroipm2.adobe.com`), and internal AD/domain traffic (LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos/SMB2 to 10.2.28.2, WPAD lookups for `easyas123.tech`/`mshome.net`) are normal enterprise background noise and are not part of the compromise.
